genericResult.narrative: The 12-lead ECG has been obtained and reviewed.
High-sensitivity troponin I is within normal limits (<52 ng/L).
The chest X-ray has been completed and reviewed.
ABG shows no significant acid-base disturbance.
CBC is within normal limits.
Basic chemistries are within normal limits.
LDL is elevated at 145 mg/dL. HDL is below the optimal threshold. Triglycerides are borderline high.
Normal left ventricular function. Ejection fraction 60%. No significant valvular abnormality.
Urine pregnancy test is positive, confirming the presence of hCG. Sensitivity threshold ~25 mIU/mL.

Quantitative serum β-hCG is 1,800 mIU/mL. This is below the typical transvaginal ultrasound discriminatory zone (~3,000 mIU/mL), but a gestational sac should be visible at this level with TVUS if IUP.
Transvaginal ultrasound has been performed.
Transabdominal ultrasound has been performed.

genericResult.summary: Blood type and Rh: O negative
genericResult.narrative: Patient is O negative. Rh immunisation prophylaxis (Rho(D) immune globulin) is indicated after any bleeding event in an Rh-negative pregnancy.
Serum progesterone 8 ng/mL. Levels <5 ng/mL suggest non-viable pregnancy; >25 ng/mL strongly suggests viable IUP. This intermediate value is non-diagnostic alone.
Urinalysis: clear urine, no leukocyte esterase, no nitrites, WBC 0-2/hpf. No evidence of urinary tract infection.
Urine culture sent. Preliminary result pending — final sensitivity results in 48–72 hours.
Two sets of blood cultures collected from separate sites before antibiotic administration. Preliminary results pending 48–72 hours.
Sputum sent for gram stain and culture. Preliminary report: gram-positive diplococci — consistent with Streptococcus pneumoniae. Full sensitivity pending.
CRP 8.2 mg/L (reference <5 mg/L). Mildly elevated — consistent with early or mild inflammatory response. Does not reliably distinguish viral from bacterial infection.
Serum lactate 1.6 mmol/L (normal <2 mmol/L). No evidence of tissue hypoperfusion at this time.

Procalcitonin 0.8 ng/mL. Values ≥0.25 ng/mL suggest bacterial infection; ≥0.5 ng/mL supports antibiotic initiation; values >2 suggest more severe bacterial infection or sepsis. This result supports a bacterial aetiology.
Multiplex respiratory viral PCR: Influenza A/B negative, RSV negative, SARS-CoV-2 negative. No common respiratory viruses detected. Result supports a bacterial rather than viral aetiology.
Cardiotocograph applied. Continuous fetal heart rate and uterine activity monitoring in progress.
Coagulation screen within normal limits. PT/INR 1.1, APTT 32 seconds, fibrinogen 3.2 g/L.
Blood group A positive. No atypical red cell antibodies detected. Sample held for crossmatch — 2 units compatible packed red cells available within 20 minutes.

Urinalysis (cystocentesis sample): Amber, cloudy urine. Leukocyte esterase 3+, nitrites positive, blood 3+, protein 1+. Specific gravity 1.042 (concentrated). Sediment exam: 42 WBCs/hpf, 18 RBCs/hpf, many rod-shaped bacteria. Findings are highly consistent with bacterial urinary tract infection.
Urine culture submitted from cystocentesis sample. Preliminary report pending 3–5 days. Culture-guided therapy enables targeted antibiotic selection and reduces resistance pressure.

CBC: Mild leukocytosis (14.2 × 10³/µL) with neutrophilia (10.8 × 10³/µL) — consistent with active bacterial infection. Haematocrit 35% (low-normal for cats; reference 30–45%). Platelets normal. Results support a localised bacterial process.

Chemistry panel: BUN 28 mg/dL and creatinine 1.2 mg/dL are within normal feline reference ranges (BUN 14–36, Cr 0.6–2.4 mg/dL). Liver values normal. Glucose mildly elevated — likely stress hyperglycaemia (common in cats). Renal function intact; no evidence of upper tract involvement or azotaemia.

Abdominal ultrasound (focused bladder/kidneys): Urinary bladder — mild wall thickening (3.5 mm; normal <1.7 mm), increased echogenicity of bladder contents, no uroliths (stones) identified. Urethra not obstructed. Kidneys — bilateral normal size and echogenicity; no pyelonephritis signs. No free abdominal fluid. Findings consistent with cystitis without urolithiasis or upper tract extension.

Ear cytology (right ear canal, Diff-Quik stained): Heavy Malassezia yeast — 15–20 'footprint-shaped' organisms per high-power field (diagnostic threshold >5/hpf with signs). Occasional non-significant cocci. Moderate degenerate neutrophils confirming active inflammation. No rod-shaped bacteria, no ear mites. Diagnosis: Malassezia otitis externa.

Ear swab culture submitted. Preliminary: Malassezia pachydermatis — heavy growth. Susceptible to miconazole, clotrimazole, ketoconazole. No significant bacterial growth (contaminant level). Results confirm cytology: pure yeast infection, azole antifungals appropriate.

CBC: WBC 9.8 × 10³/µL — normal. Mild borderline eosinophilia (0.9 × 10³/µL; ref 0–0.9) — possible atopic contribution but not diagnostic alone. Haematocrit 46% — normal. Platelets normal. No significant leukocytosis or anaemia.
Chemistry: Hepatic and renal values normal. T4 2.4 µg/dL (normal 1.0–4.0) — hypothyroidism unlikely as a primary driver. All values within reference ranges. No systemic disease identified.
